parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence is documented: the buggery/indecency provisions were sexuality-law, secondary here, and were repealed island-wide in 2024. Nothing records presentation offences, police targeting, document scrutiny, facility or custody rules, or violence against trans visitors — an open question, not an exposure. Positive evidence exists: the fakafifine tradition is documented as cultural heritage, and the assembly recently removed colonial offences, signalling a functioning, reforming legal order. No universal-exposure measure (tier 1) or organised targeting (tier 2) appears. Deductions: no documented visitor-facing protections or recourse, no hate-crime/anti-discrimination coverage, marriage non-recognition is resident-facing and not counted, and the dossier is thin on border, facilities, and custody practice — so acceptance is plausible but not institutionally demonstrated. That places it a step below acceptance-with-working-protections.
